classification.difficultyReason: Read the labelled x-intercept and translate the graph's positions below and above the x-axis into strict inequalities.

content.prompt: The diagram below shows the graph of $y=x+2$. Use your graph to solve the following.

spec.description: Rising blue line with arrows at both ends; positive-axis arrows and labels; only the x-intercept has a numerical tick label. Source blue is mapped to the standard blue graph accent.
spec.mathematics: The line is y=x+2 and crosses the x-axis at x=-2. There is no grid.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph and its printed intercept label remain visible in the student edition.

answer.worked: The graph crosses the $x$-axis at $x=-2$, where $y=0$. Hence $x=-2$.
The graph is below the $x$-axis to the left of $x=-2$. Hence $x<-2$; the intercept is excluded because the inequality is strict.
The graph is above the $x$-axis to the right of $x=-2$. Hence $x>-2$; the intercept is excluded because the inequality is strict.
